text.en:
1. (1) This Act may be cited as the Human Tissues Act, Short

1974 and shall apply throughout Malaysia.                 application.
(2) This Act shall come into force on such date as the

Minister responsible for health may by notification in the

Gazette appoint.

2. (1) If any person, either in writing at any time or orally Removal of
in the presence of two or more witnesses during his last Parisol
illness, has expressed a request that his body or any specified therapeutic
part of his body be used after his death for therapeutic PUPoses.
purposes, or for purposes of medical education or research,
the person lawfully in possession of his body after his death
may, unless he has reason to believe that the request was
subsequently withdrawn, authorise the removal from the
body of any part or, as the case may be, the specified part,
for use in accordance with the request.

(2) Without prejudice to the foregoing subsection, the
person lawfully in possession of the body of a deceased
person may authorise the removal of any part from the said
body for use for the purposes aforesaid if, having made
such reasonable enquiry as may be practicable, he has no
reason to believe—

(a) that the deceased had expressed an objection to his
body being so dealt with after his death; or

(b) that the surviving spouse or any surviving next-of-
kin of the deceased objects to the body being so
dealt with.

(3) No authorisation shall be given under this section in
respect of any body by a person entrusted with the body
for the purpose only of its internment or cremation.

3. (1) Subject to subsections (2) and (3), the removal and
use of any part of a body in accordance with an authorisa-
tion given in pursuance of section 2 shall be lawful.

(2) No such removal shall be effected except by a medical
practitioner fully registered under section 14 of the Medical
Act, 1971, and who together with at least one other fully
registered medical practitioner have satisfied themselves by
personal examination of the body that life is extinct.

(3) Where a person has reason to believe that a post-
mortem, or an inquest or an inquiry into the death, may be
held under the Criminal Procedure Code applicable, he shall
not except with the written consent of the Magistrate—

(a) give authorisation under section 2 in respect of the
body; or

(b) act on an authorisation given by the deceased under
section 2 (1) or by any other person.

4, In the case of a body of a deceased person lying in a
hospital and unclaimed the person having the control and
management of the hospital or any other person authorised
by him shall be deemed for the purpose of this Act to be a
person in lawful possession of the body.

5. Nothing in this Act shall be construed as rendering
unlawful any dealing with, or with any part of, the body
of a deceased person which could have been lawful if this
Act had not been passed.
